en: The Apadāna of the Elder Maggadattika Kumuda Chapter, Number 6 I was once a merchant’s son, named Maggadattika, In the city of Benares, a place of great renown. There, I saw the Buddha, the Teacher, the One with Vision, The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One. Having seen him, I took up a path of earth, And spread it out for the sake of the Great Sage. Then, having performed that act of merit, I spoke these words to the Teacher: “O Blessed One, may you be well; May you be free from illness and suffering. May you be at ease, O Blessed One; May you be free from illness and suffering. Having spoken thus to the Teacher, I then departed from his presence. At the end of my life, I passed away, And was reborn in the realm of Tusita. From there, I passed away and was reborn In the human world, in a wealthy family. There, I was known as Maggadattika, A man of great wealth and prosperity. When I reached the age of twenty, I went forth into homelessness. Having gone forth, I practiced the holy life Under the guidance of the Teacher. For eighty-four thousand years, I lived the life of a celibate monk. I maintained the precepts perfectly, Without any breach or flaw. Having observed the holy life With such purity and diligence, I passed away at the end of my time And was reborn in the Brahma world. There, I dwelt for a full aeon, Enjoying celestial bliss. From there, I passed away and was reborn In the human world, in a wealthy family. Once again, I was known as Maggadattika, Endowed with great wealth and power. When I reached the age of twenty, I went forth into homelessness. lord of bipeds, bull among men,
for the sake of happiness in this very life...”
He paced back and forth in the open air.
As his feet were lifted up, flowers remained clinging to the soles of his feet;
as he stood, they remained upon his head.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
I paid homage and scattered flowers.
From here [in the past], there were five persons named Pupphacchadaniya,
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Maggadattika spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Maggadattika.
